rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The chief aim is to warn all creatures away from ruinous obedience to devils, who turned people from their original upright faith.
rows.anchor: المقصود الأعظم به النذارة لكف الخلائق عما يثمر الهلاك من اتباع الشياطين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Warning near relatives implies warning everyone else a fortiori and softens distant people’s pride by addressing them as kin.
rows.anchor: وإنذار الأقربين يفهم الإنذار لغيرهم من باب الأولى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Bukhari reports from Ibn Abbas that the Prophet called Quraysh clans to Ṣafā, asked whether they would believe a warning of approaching cavalry, then warned of punishment; Abu Lahab cursed him, and Sūrat al-Masad followed.
rows.anchor: روى البخاري عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: In a version, the Prophet warns Quraysh, Banu Abd Manaf, Abbas, Safiyya, and Fatima that he cannot save them from God, though Fatima may ask for worldly property.
rows.anchor: يا معشر قريش ! اشتروا أنفسكم , لا أغني عنكم من الله شيئا

rows.speaker: الزبير بن العوام
rows.claim: Abu Yaʿlā reports from al-Zubayr that Quraysh demanded miracles including Solomon’s wind, David’s mountains, Moses’ sea, Jesus’ reviving the dead, moving mountains, flowing rivers, and turning rock to gold; God revealed they would disbelieve and be punished, so the Prophet chose patience in hope of mercy.
rows.anchor: روى القصة أبو يعلى عن الزبير بن العوام رضي الله عنه أن قريشا جاءته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lowering the wing means utmost gentleness: a bird lowers its wings when descending, making the image a figure for humility.
rows.anchor: لأن الطائر إذا أراد أن يرتفه رفع جناحيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The form of ittibāʿ may avoid including Abu Talib, who did not believe, only professed belief hypocritically, or was a sinful person of weak faith.
rows.anchor: ولعله احترز بالتعبير بصيغة الافتعال عن مثل أبي طالب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The qualifier identifies those whose faith is an established trait, whether they are near or distant relatives.
rows.anchor: أي الذين صار الإيمان لهمصفة راسخة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If these believers disobey, others are included a fortiori; the Prophet must cease the gentleness shown to them as believers and disavow their sinful conduct.
rows.anchor: أي هم فغيرهم من باب الأولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disavowal is complete separation from their disobedience, the conduct the Qur’an warned against.
rows.anchor: أي منفصل غاية الانفصال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naming the believers honors them; the wording lets a wavering person recognize their standing and encourages him to join them.
rows.anchor: وخص المؤمنين إعلاء لمقامهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Trust God for protection, deliverance, and turning those warned toward obedience.
rows.anchor: أي في عصمتك ونجاتك والإقبال بالمنذرين إلى الطاعة

rows.speaker: أهل المدينة والشام
rows.claim: Medinan and Syrian readers use the causal fāʾ, which more clearly links trust to the preceding command; other readers have wāw.
rows.anchor: وقراءة أهل المدينة والشام بالفاء السببية أدل على ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Mighty can protect the Prophet and take vengeance on opponents; the Merciful is hoped to honor everyone by ending discord and employing them in what pleases Him.
rows.anchor: أي القادر على الدفع عنكم والانتقام منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The description following the trust command establishes God’s sufficiency: His encompassing knowledge secures every benefit and repels every harm.
rows.anchor: بما يقتضي الكفاية في كل ما ينوب من دفع الضر وجلب النفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sees the Prophet with sight and knowledge as he rises from bed after sleep, leaving its comfort for God’s pleasure.
rows.anchor: من نومك من فرشك تاركا لحبك , لأجل رضا ربك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sees the Prophet’s changing prayer postures, standing and prostrating among his believing followers.
rows.anchor: اي المصلين من أتباعك المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believers recite with a sound like bees, supplicate in fear, sigh, and weep; their devotion merits divine favor.
rows.anchor: لكم دوي بالقرآن ادوي النحل

rows.speaker: البغوي
rows.claim: Al-Baghawī reports that some define a flame as a column-like luminous thing, and Arabs call any white luminous object a flame; a qabas is a piece of fire.
rows.anchor: وقال البغوي : وقال بعضهم : الشهاب شيء ذو نور مثل العمود

rows.speaker: الكوفيون
rows.claim: Kufian readers vocalize shihāban with nunation and construe qabas as apposition or description.
rows.anchor: فقراءة الكوفيين بالتنوين على البدل أو الوصف

rows.speaker: غيرهم
rows.claim: Other readers use a genitive construction because qabas is the more specific term.
rows.anchor: وقراءة غيرهم بالإضافة , لأن القبس أخص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It was a cold night, so Moses hoped the fire would warm his family on his return.
rows.anchor: لأنها ليله باردة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object Moses reached was what he had taken to be a fire.
rows.anchor: أي تلك التي ظنها نارا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The call is expressed in the passive, with God as the caller.
rows.anchor: اي من قبل الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unspecified call first creates suspense; the clarification directs the hearer to infer the greatness of the event.
rows.anchor: ولما كان البيان بعد الإبهام أعظم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording signals that the call is clarified by what follows because calling here has the force of saying.
rows.anchor: لأن النداء بمعنى القول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To bless is to establish flourishing that brings increase, purity, and every describable good.
rows.anchor: أي ثبت تثبيتا يحصل منه من النماء والطهارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase may refer to the fire’s location or to the person seeking it, with the latter functioning as supplication.
rows.anchor: أي بقعتها , أو طلبها وهو طلب بمعنى الدعاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account suggests a large tree: as Moses approached, the fire moved away and he followed it into the ravine, where light surrounded him; the light is called fire after his first impression.
rows.anchor: العبارة تدل على أن الشجرة كانت كبيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The radiance, though called fire, may have been light because Moses first thought he saw fire.
rows.anchor: وسمي النور نارا على ما كان في ظن موسى

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr says the fire was actual, as Moses saw it.
rows.anchor: سعيد بن جبير : بل كانت نارا

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The cited hadith says God’s veil is fire, and if He uncovered it, the splendors of His face would burn whatever His sight reaches.
rows.anchor: كما في الحديث : ( حجابه النار لو كشفها لأحرقت سبحات وجهه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those around the fire include all angels and the sacred lands, then and whenever God wills.
rows.anchor: من جميع الملائكة عليهم السلام وتلك الأراضي المقدسة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sacred lands deserve this status because prophets were sent there, revelation descended there, and prophets were laid to rest there.
rows.anchor: لأنها مبعث الأنبياء عليهم الصلاة والسلام ومهبط الوحي عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The call came from every direction and Moses heard it through all his senses.
rows.anchor: من جميع الجهات , فسمعه بجميع الحواس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The context implies a command to rejoice at this great glad tiding and glorify the perfectly complete King in a manner befitting His majesty.
rows.anchor: أي ونزه الملك الذي له الكمال المطلق تنزيها يليق بجلاله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the phrase is a predicate coordinated with “blessed”: God is transcendent and is not located at the place of the call or anywhere else.
rows.anchor: أي وتنزه الله سبحانه تنزها يليق بجلاله عن أن يكون في موضع النداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling God Lord of the worlds shows He deserves sanctification through His perfect essence and acts toward creatures, including raising Moses as an adult after raising him as a child.
rows.anchor: التي منها ما يريد أن يربي به موسى عليه الصلاة والسلام كبيرا بعد ما رباه به صغيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s identity declares a majesty beyond the reach of imagination or understanding.
rows.anchor: أي البالغ من العظمة ما تقصر عنه الأوهام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Mighty reaches whatever He wills, and nothing He possesses can be reached except by the route He chooses.
rows.anchor: أي الذي يصل إلى جميع ما يريد ولا يوصل إلى شيء مما عنده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Wise can undo what others do when He wills, while no one can undo any of His acts.
rows.anchor: أي الذي ينقص كل ما يفعله غيره إذا أراد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Throwing the staff lets Moses witness God’s might and wisdom; alternatively, the command coordinates with the earlier blessing announcement.
rows.anchor: لتعلم علما شهوديا عزتي وحكمتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The staff became a huge, exceptionally light and swift serpent, writhing as it pursued what it wanted.
rows.anchor: فصارت في الحال - بما أذنت به الفاء - حية عظيمة جدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jānn refers to a small snake in lightness and speed; this does not contradict the serpent’s large body.
rows.anchor: أي حية صغيرة في خفتها وسرعتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses turned and fled from the serpent at great speed.
rows.anchor: اي التفت هاربا منها مسرعا جدا لقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He did not turn back, hesitate in fleeing, or look behind him.
rows.anchor: أي لم يرجع على عقبه , ولم يتردد في الجد في الهرب

rows.speaker: المحكم
rows.claim: Al-Muḥkam gives ʿaqaba on someone the sense of turning back, and ʿaqaba in a matter the sense of persisting in pursuit.
rows.anchor: تردد في طلبه مجدا - هذا في ترتيب المحكم

rows.speaker: القاموس
rows.claim: Al-Qāmūs gives taʿqīb the sense of looking back.
rows.anchor: وفي القاموس : التعقيب : الالتفات

rows.speaker: القزاز
rows.claim: Al-Qazzāz’s dictionary defines ʿaqaba as turning back after departing.
rows.anchor: وقال القزاز في ديوانه : عقب - إذا انصرف راجعا فهو معقب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God answers Moses’ fear with reassurance and a promise of safety.
rows.anchor: ولما تشوفت النفس غلى ما قيل له عند هذه الحالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “In My presence” means the extraordinary setting and time of revelation.
rows.anchor: أي في الموضع الذي هو من غرائب نواقض العادات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Messengers are protected from injustice, and only a wrongdoer fears a just ruler.
rows.anchor: ولا يخاف من الملك العدل إلا ظالم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Having seen that a ruler who commands the birds is impossible to defeat or outwit, the queen turns toward peace.
rows.anchor: لا يعجزه شيء يريده , ولا أحد بكيده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After her advisers’ answer revealed an inclination to fight, she judges the safest course is avoiding war with this powerful king.
rows.anchor: في جوابهم من ميلهم إلى الحرب أن الصواب من غير ارتياب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kings generally enter towns by force; the queen says this powerful king would be especially formidable.
rows.anchor: فكيف بهذا النافذ الأمر , العظيم القدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kings ruin towns through plunder and destruction and humble their notables by displaying power and inflicting force.
rows.anchor: أفسدوها } أي بالنهب والتخريب { وجعلوا اعزة قومها اذلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Her “that is how they act” stresses that this is kings’ regular, shared, enduring practice.
rows.anchor: هو خلق لهم مستمر جميعهم على هذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She chooses conciliation by sending a gift to the king and his soldiers, intended as a courteous overture.
rows.anchor: اي إليه وإلى جنوده { بهدية } أي تقع منهم موقعا

rows.speaker: البغوي
rows.claim: Al-Baghawī defines the gift as a present offered as a friendly overture.
rows.anchor: قال البغوي : وهي العطية على طريق الملاطفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She will assess what the messengers bring back in words or appearance, then decide what to do, avoiding a premature confrontation.
rows.anchor: بتلك الهدية عنه من المقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An account says the gift included 500 boys dressed as girls and instructed to speak as girls, and 500 girls dressed as boys and instructed to speak as boys, plus a crooked gem and an unpierced pearl.
rows.anchor: خمسمائة غلام مرد , زينتهم بزي الجواري , وأمرتهم بتأنيث الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The queen asks Solomon to distinguish the boys from girls, pierce the pearl, and thread the crooked hole.
rows.anchor: وسألته أن يميز بين الغلمان والجواري , وأن يثقب الدرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The girl transfers water between her hands, slaps her face, and pours it inside her forearm; the boy throws water on his face and pours it over the back of his arm.
rows.anchor: فأمرهم بغسل الوجوه والأيدي , فكانت الجارية تأخذ الماء بإحدى يديها ثم تنقله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Solomon uses a termite to bore the pearl and a worm to pass a thread through the crooked hole.
rows.anchor: وأمر الأرضة فثقبت الدرة , والدودة فأدخلت السلك

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān notes that rasūl can refer to a group or an individual, and can be masculine or feminine.
rows.anchor: قال أبو حيان : وهو يقع على الجمع والمفرد والمذكر والمؤنث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The envoy delivered the gift; Solomon addressed the messenger, his entourage, and the sender, treating the offering as insignificant.
rows.anchor: أي الرسول الذي بعثته وارسلته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Solomon says his purpose in approaching them was religion; worldly wealth has no appeal and nothing short of obedience to God satisfies him.
rows.anchor: وإنما قصدي لكم لأجل الدين

words: فَمَآ ءَاتَىٰنِۦَ ٱللَّهُ خَيْرٌۭ مِّمَّآ ءَاتَىٰكُم
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s gifts of prophethood, kingship, and closeness are better than their wealth; whoever obeys God is enriched by His gifts.
rows.anchor: بالنبوة والملك والقب منه سبحانه

words: فَمَآ ءَاتَىٰنِۦَ ٱللَّهُ خَيْرٌۭ مِّمَّآ ءَاتَىٰكُم
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As evidence of extraordinary rule, Solomon arrayed jinn, humans, predators, wild animals, birds, and vermin in ranks for miles and spread the place with soft gold.
rows.anchor: صف الشياطين والإنس والسباع والوحش والطير والهوام صفوفا فراسخ عدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading is that ignorance makes them value worldly goods and suppose a gift will turn Solomon from them.
rows.anchor: بجهلكم لذلك تستعظمون ما أنتم فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, they rejoice at gifts received and abandon their planned campaign against the recipients of worldly goods, while Solomon seeks only religion.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يراد أنكم تفرحون بما يهدي إليكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Solomon’s state is unlike theirs: he is satisfied only by religion.
rows.anchor: فحالي خلاف حالكم , فإنه لا يرضيني إلا الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He addresses the envoy in the singular as the queen’s chief, then uses plural wording to honor her, avoid explicitly pronouncing her pronoun, and include those concerned with and obedient to her.
rows.anchor: إرادة لكبيرهم بقوله : { ارجع } وجمع في قوله : { إليهم }

words: فَلَنَأْتِيَنَّهُم بِجُنُودٍ لَّا قِبَلَ لَهُم بِهَا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They have no capacity to face Solomon’s forces or turn them aside from their purpose.
rows.anchor: لا قبل } أي طاقة { لهم بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They will be driven from their land humiliated; “abased” means they will have no defense unless they submit to Islam.
rows.anchor: ولما كان الذل قد يكون لمجرد الانقياد , لا على سبيلالهوان

words: قَالَ يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلْمَلَؤُا۟ أَيُّكُمْ يَأْتِينِى بِعَرْشِهَا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the envoys leave, Solomon sees from their awe that the queen will come submissively and asks his assembly to bring her throne.
rows.anchor: من تصاغرهم لما رأوا من هيبته وجلاله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Displaying a divine marvel may help her accept faith; Solomon also wants the throne before her submission makes taking it impermissible and to test her intelligence.
rows.anchor: لترى بعض ما تاني الله من الخوارق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “They come to me” means the queen and her people; “Muslim” means yielding to his rule and abandoning sovereignty, helping establish his prophethood and their sincere faith.
rows.anchor: منقادين لسلطاني , تاركين لعز سلطانهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God empowers the Israelites throughout the earth, especially Egypt and Syria, by destroying their enemies and supporting them through Moses and later prophets, angels, and miracles.
rows.anchor: أي كلها لا سيما أرض مصر والشام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh is the persecutor, Haman his minister, and their soldiers agents of their corruption; the Israelites bring them what they continually fear: loss of rule through an Israelite child.
rows.anchor: أي الذي كان هذا الاستضعاف منه

rows.speaker: البغوي
rows.claim: Al-Baghawī defines ḥadhar as guarding oneself against harm.
rows.anchor: قال البغوي : والحذر : التوقي من الضرر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse uses ihtibāk: oppression first implies later strength, while the later feared outcome implies earlier beneficence, comforting listeners and encouraging patient hope for relief.
rows.anchor: والآية من الاحتباك : ذكر الاستضعاف أولا دليلا على القوة ثانيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh slaughtered Israelite sons to prevent the feared child’s rise, but God arranged for Moses to be born and raised in the household Pharaoh feared.
rows.anchor: فأولدنا من بني إسرائيل الولد الذي كان يحذره فرعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The revelation reached Moses’ mother through a hidden means, whether angel or otherwise; there is nothing impossible in angels addressing a non-prophet saint.
rows.anchor: إذ لا بدع في تكليم الملائكة الولي من غير نبوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She is told to nurse Moses while safe; if she fears he will cry, be heard, and killed, she should place him in a water-safe container and cast him into the Nile.
rows.anchor: أي منهم أن يصيح فيسمع فيذبح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-yamm means sea, but here is the Nile; its size and benefits make the name apt, while yamm emphasizes the intended destination more than breadth.
rows.anchor: البحر - لعظمته على غيره من الأنهار بكبره

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī describes trust in three degrees: ceasing to resist decrees, confidence that destiny cannot be lost—yielding contentment, certainty, or patience—and direct witnessing of God that releases attachment to goals and means.
rows.anchor: قال الرازي في اللوامع : وهذا إشارة إلى الثقة بالله

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: The first degree is despair of changing the divine apportionment; the second is security from losing what is decreed; the third is direct witnessing of God beyond trials of desired outcomes and reliance on means.
rows.anchor: ولها درجات : الأولى درجة الأياس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She need not fear drowning, death from the end of nursing even after a long interval, or any harm reaching the child.
rows.anchor: أي لا يتجدد لك خوف أصلا من أن يغرق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She need not grieve the separation from her son.
rows.anchor: أي ولا يوجد لك حزن لوقوع فراقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fear concerns what may happen, while grief concerns what has already happened.
rows.anchor: ولماكان الخوف عما يلحق المتوقعن والحزن عما يلحق الواقع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic nominal sentence conveys a permanent promise and removes the cause of both fear and grief.
rows.anchor: دالة علىالثبات والدوام , مؤكدة لاستبعاد مضمونها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God adds the greatest glad tiding: Moses will be among the finest of creation, the messengers.
rows.anchor: أي الذين هم خلاصة المخلوقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse uses ihtibāk: nursing implies she will later stop nursing, while later fear implies earlier safety; it reassures her by naming what she loves.
rows.anchor: ذكر الإرضاع أولا دليلا على تركه ثانيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After nursing him, his mother sealed him in a waterproof, pitch-coated chest and cast it into the Nile; the current carried it near Pharaoh’s house, where a tree caught it and his people found it.
rows.anchor: صنعت له صندوقا وقيرته لئلا يدخل إليه الماء

rows.speaker: البغوي
rows.claim: Al-Baghawī explains iltiqāṭ as finding something without having sought it.
rows.anchor: قال البغوي : والالتقاط وجود الشيء من غير طلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh’s household found the chest and loved Moses because God placed love for him in their hearts, then adopted him.
rows.anchor: فاتخذوه ولدا وسموه موسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account says they named him Moses because they found him in water and tree; mu meant water and sā tree in their language.
rows.anchor: ومو بلسانهم : الماء , وسا : الشجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses would oppose them by rejecting their religion and calling them to truth, and grieve them through loss of kingdom and destruction.
rows.anchor: أي بطول خوفهم منه بمخالفته لهم في دينهم وحملهم على الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses’ signs would destroy those God willed, kill the Egyptian firstborn and free Israel, then bring a drowning that grieved the whole region.
rows.anchor: ثم يهلك جميع أبكارهم فيخلص جميع بني إسرائيل منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purpose lām is ironic: the family is said to have taken Moses for this end, though they could not knowingly adopt the child who would destroy them; the comparison likens him to a lion.
rows.anchor: فهذه اللام للعلة استعيرت الأسد للشجاع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh, Haman, and their troops shared one disposition, so it is unsurprising they raised the Israelite child they feared while slaughtering Israelite sons.
rows.anchor: أي كلهم على طبع واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their habit was deliberate sinning and straying from right aims, explaining their foolish treatment of Moses and false claim to divinity.
rows.anchor: أي دابهم تعمد الذنوب , والضلال عن المقاصد

rows.speaker: أبو عبيد
rows.claim: Abū ʿUbayd treats akhṭaʾa and khaṭiʾa as two dialect forms with the same meaning.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبيد : أخطأ وخطأ - لغتان بمعنى واحد

rows.speaker: ابن عرفة
rows.claim: Ibn ʿArafa says both expressions can describe following a mistaken path, intentionally or unintentionally.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عرفة : يقال

rows.speaker: الأموي
rows.claim: Al-Amwī distinguishes someone who misses despite aiming at what is right from someone who deliberately does what ought not be done.
rows.anchor: وقال الأموي , المخطىء من أراد الصواب فصار إلى غيره

rows.speaker: ابن ظريف
rows.claim: Ibn Ẓarīf glosses khaṭiʾa or akhṭaʾahu as failing to hit or attain something.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن ظريف في الأفعال : خطىء الشيء خطأ وأخطأه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account briefly gives the ending before returning to Pharaoh’s household, framing the story with their error and arousing interest in its details.
rows.anchor: بجمع طرفي القصة إجمالا وتشويقا إلى تفصيل ذلك الإجمال

rows.speaker: البغوي
rows.claim: Al-Baghawī identifies Pharaoh’s wife as Āsiya bint Muzāḥim, described here as an Israelite woman.
rows.anchor: وهي آسية بنت مزاحم إحدى نساء بني إسرائيل - نقله البغوي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She tells Pharaoh the child is a joy to both of them.
rows.anchor: أي به { ولك } أي يا فرعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She asks that neither Pharaoh nor anyone he commands kill the child.
rows.anchor: أي أنت بنفسك ولا أحد ممن تأمره بذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She fears Pharaoh might offer to spare the child merely to appease her, then kill him while avoiding a broken promise.
rows.anchor: فيجيبها حاملا له على الحقيقة ثم يأمر بقتله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She hopes the child’s apparent nobility will make him useful, or that they can adopt him if his parents are unknown, bringing royal honor.
rows.anchor: وهو جدير وخليق { أن ينفعنا } أي لما أتخيل فيه النجابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their words expose ignorance and disprove Pharaoh’s divinity; they do not grasp what Moses will bring or the destruction coming to them, nor discipline themselves to gain knowledge.
rows.anchor: ولما كان هذا كله فعل من لا يعلم , فلا يصح كونه إلها
